title: cairn cleanup clears a terminal ticket's own unqueued and refused troubles
intention: bin/cmd/cleanup gains a tickets step before the drain: it hands the live ticket-unqueued-* and ticket-refused-* trouble ids to python3 -m cairn.machines.ticket.ticket --recheck, and the ticket machine's new recheck() has each ticket that stands at a terminal state, with the raise standing on its own trail, emit clear_trouble for it; the drain folds the clears.
why: Measured 2026-11-19: ticket-unqueued-8c5fdb750b75-at-clearance stands live although 8c5fdb750b75 is PROVED. Its two clearance asks timed out (11-18 11:04 and 11:06) while the gate still carried it to PROVED, and the trouble clears only when a later ask at the same gate is taken (41a5bae3d01b) or passed (794835a34ec9). A terminal ticket asks no gate again, so nothing is left to clear it. Ticket 17b087f2483f's bounds named this as its sibling ticket at cairn/machines/ticket.
traces_to: Law 7: a record of truth stays true. A trouble that stands after its cause is gone tells the inbox reader something false, and the drain cannot fold a clear nobody sends.
how: Add recheck(ids, *, tickets_dir=None, roots=None) to cairn/machines/ticket/ticket.py. It parses ticket-(unqueued|refused)-<tid>-at-<gate>, resolves the ticket with Ticket.at, and clears the trouble when is_terminal(cursor state) and _stands_raised(identity) both hold. It returns {cleared, standing, unknown}. Add a __main__ --recheck <ids...> [--tickets-dir, default $CAIRN_TICKETS_DIR] that calls the named module's recheck, never __main__'s, because a Ticket built under __main__ names its trail after __main__. Add a tickets step to bin/cmd/cleanup between seals and troubles, and add 'tickets' to --summarize's counted names. The red-first proof is cairn/machines/ticket/proofs/test_a_terminal_ticket_clears_its_ticket_troubles.py.

clauses.claim: a ticket at PROVED whose unqueued trouble stands raised: recheck clears it, and the newest record naming it on the ticket's trail is the clear
a ticket still under way (FIXME) keeps its raised trouble, and a terminal ticket with nothing raised is sent no clear: both read standing
in a scratch HOME, a PROVED ticket's unqueued trouble is drained OPEN, bin/cairn cleanup's tickets line reports it cleared, and cairn trouble live no longer lists it

decisions.text: D1: the ticket machine clears its own troubles; terminal means workflow_grammar.is_terminal on the cursor state, and the raise must stand on the ticket's own trail (_stands_raised), so a ticket that raised nothing sends nothing.

D2: cleanup reaches the ticket machine as a subprocess CLI (python3 -m cairn.machines.ticket.ticket --recheck), the same shape as the findings and seals steps; the CLI calls the named module's recheck so the trail is the ticket's own, not __main__'s.

D3: the proof is red-first: teeth 1 and 2 run recheck in-process over a scratch store and scratch roots, and tooth 3 runs bin/cairn cleanup in a scratch HOME with CAIRN_TICKETS_DIR at the store and its own CAIRN_BUS_UNIT, stopped and reset-failed in finally.

out: the seal-red and finding troubles (17b087f2483f, the inspector)
a refused trouble on a ticket still under way (it clears when its gate passes)

measured.saw: ticket-unqueued-8c5fdb750b75-at-clearance live while 8c5fdb750b75 is PROVED; read-only probe: _step PROVED, _stands_raised True; 287e241f61f3 and 0c2c3f53c2be read FIXME and would stand
measured.how: cairn trouble live; Ticket.at(...)._stands_raised over the live store, read only

measured.saw: the drafted proof: red at HEAD (ImportError on recheck; tooth 3 red); red with the cleanup tickets step removed (tooth 3); red with the __main__ CLI removed (tooth 3); green twice as built
measured.how: bin/cairn test <proof> in worktree ticket-troubles-terminal, each revert restored from a saved copy

measured.saw: the CLI first read every id standing: under python -m the Ticket class is __main__'s and its trail is named after __main__
